get.summary: A public document the provider fetches, such as client metadata

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
Sign out of the current session
Set a new password with a one-time link

post.description: Sets a new password after checking the current one. Every other session of the user is signed out; this one stays and counts as just re-authenticated. Accounts with two-factor sign-in are refused (422 `two_factor_unavailable`) until a second-factor check exists. A wrong current password is 422 and counts towards the same five-failure lockout as re-authentication; the fifth revokes this session (401).
Refreshes the session's re-authentication time, which approving needs within the last 12 h. The session token stays the same. Five wrong passwords since the last confirmation revoke the session.
post.summary: Confirm the password for the current session

get.summary: The signed-in user and their workspaces

patch.description: Changes the signed-in user's own display name and the language their emails use. Send at least one field. The name is trimmed; null or an empty string clears it.

get.description: Plain text in English, Slovak or Czech, chosen from Accept-Language.
get.summary: Status of a Meta data deletion request

post.description: Meta posts a signed request when a person removes the app. Their channels on that network need reconnecting and their tokens are deleted. Called by Meta, not by API clients.

Meta posts a signed request when a person asks to delete their data. Their channels on that network are disconnected and wiped in every workspace; the answer links to a status page. Called by Meta, not by API clients.

get.summary: Finish connecting a channel after the provider redirects back

get.description: The workspace policy (null when there is none), the brand overrides, and the policy that applies to a post without a brand. With no workspace policy the strictest default applies: approval required, no self-approval, tolerance 0.

put.description: Owners and admins only. Existing approval requests and destinations keep what they were bound to: a stricter policy applies when a destination is claimed, a looser one never approves anything by itself. A stale expectedVersion is 409.

delete.description: The brand's posts fall back to the workspace policy. Owners and admins only; 404 when the brand has no override.
delete.summary: Remove a brand's approval policy override

put.description: Owners and admins only. Existing approval requests and destinations keep what they were bound to: a stricter policy applies when a destination is claimed, a looser one never approves anything by itself. A stale expectedVersion is 409. 404 when the brand is not in the workspace.
put.summary: Set a brand's approval policy override

post.description: Records the caller's decision on an open request. Approve closes it as approved once the qualifying approvals reach the greater of the request's and the live policy's count; reject and request_changes close it as rejected.
The requester closes their own open request as withdrawn; the post goes back to an editable draft.

post.summary: Start connecting a channel through the provider

get.summary: List the providers this server can connect

post.description: The channel stops publishing; due posts to it are blocked. Where the network supports it, its access token is revoked there; its stored credentials are purged after 30 days. Connecting the same account again restores it. Owners and admins only.

get.description: The daily follower counts in [from, to] (UTC dates; default the last 30 days up to today; at most 366 days). A day is listed only when the count changed; a null value means the network did not report it. `before` is the last count before `from`, the value in effect at the start of the range.
The weekly slots (weekday 1 = Monday, local time in the queue time zone) and the next free slots that "add to queue" would take. A channel without slots has a null time zone.

put.description: Replaces every slot of the channel's queue; at most 56 slots, each weekday and time once. An empty list clears the queue and ignores the time zone. Scheduled posts never move. Owners and admins only.

get.description: The workspace's library assets that are ready or processing, not deleted and not a duplicate, newest first, optionally of one kind (image or video). limit 1–100, default 50; pass nextCursor as cursor for the next page. usageCount is the number of posts that use the asset; previewUrl is a signed URL of the image, or of a video's poster, valid for an hour.

post.description: Accepts JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 8 MiB; metadata is stripped before storage. `aiGenerated: true` marks the image as AI-generated; uploading the same image again never clears the mark.
Accepts MP4, QuickTime or WebM up to 300 MB. Send every part with `media.video_part`, then call `media.video_complete` before `expiresAt` (24 h).

delete.description: Refused with 409 media_in_use while any post uses the asset. The files are removed 30 days later.

patch.description: Sets the default alt text (trimmed, at most 1500 characters; empty or null clears it). Alt text already copied into a post doesn't change.

delete.description: Members only. Refused with 409 when the asset is not marked, or when an API key or agent uploaded or marked it.

post.description: An upload or an API key never removes the mark. Only a member can clear it, in the media library, and never for media that an API key or agent uploaded or marked.
post.summary: Mark a media asset as AI-generated

post.description: Checks that every part is present and queues the conversion. Completing again is a no-op.

put.description: Every part except the last is exactly `partSize` bytes. Sending a part again replaces it.
put.summary: Upload one part of a video

get.description: At most 50 posts, newest first. Needs posts:read as well; refused for a scoped caller.
get.summary: List the posts that use a media asset

get.description: The unconfirmed, failed, blocked and awaiting-manual destinations of the posts the caller can see, newest first (limit 1–200, default 100).

The caller's own email preferences in this workspace, per group: failures (failed, unconfirmed and awaiting-manual destinations), approvals (approval requests and decisions) and channels (reconnect and expiry warnings). true means emailed; the default is true for every group. In-app notifications are always shown.

put.description: Replaces the caller's own email preferences in this workspace; every group is required. A group set to false is no longer emailed, but its notifications still appear in-app. Returns the new preferences.

get.description: The caller's own notifications in this workspace, newest first (limit 1–100, default 50); unread=true returns unread ones only. A scoped caller gets only notifications for channels in scope. unread is the caller's total unread count.

post.description: Marks the caller's own notifications read: the listed ids (1–100), or with upTo every unread one up to and including that id (ids order to the millisecond). Ids that aren't the caller's are ignored. Returns the new unread count.

get.description: Either the posts with a destination scheduled in [from, to) (ISO instants, at most 42 days apart; at most 500 posts), or with unscheduled=true the posts with no scheduled destination, newest first (limit 1–100, default 50).

patch.description: Each field given replaces that part whole; variants and destinations replace together. Every destination must be a draft or canceled.

get.description: The 20 newest approval requests of the post, newest first, with what each bound per destination and its decisions.

post.description: Freezes every draft destination for review and opens an approval request; the destinations stay drafts. With a schedule, the approval binds that local time within the policy tolerance. With repeat (only together with a schedule; 422 invalid_repeat otherwise) the post becomes occurrence 1 of a series, and the series schedules it as the requester once the request is approved.
Cancels every destination that has not published; one that is publishing stops after its current step.
Cancels a failed, blocked or awaiting-manual destination. An unconfirmed one may already be live, so it is refused: mark it published or send it again.
Records that an unconfirmed or awaiting-manual destination is live, as a manual resolution. Parts not confirmed live are marked skipped, and a main post already live keeps its publish time.

Freezes and schedules a failed, blocked or unconfirmed destination again; parts already confirmed live are not sent twice. An unconfirmed one, or one with a part whose send was never confirmed, may already be live, so it needs acknowledgeDuplicate.

delete.description: No further copies are made. Existing copies stay as they are. 404 when the post was never marked.
delete.summary: Remove a post from the evergreen pool

get.description: Whether the post is in the evergreen pool, why it left it, and its 10 most recent copies (channel, queue slot, copy post; null once the copy is deleted). 404 when the post was never marked.

put.description: Free queue slots up to 24 h ahead are filled with copies of pool posts, at most once per channel every 30 days. The caller becomes the owner: copies are scheduled or submitted in their name. Marking a removed post again makes the caller its new owner; marking an active one changes nothing.
put.summary: Add a post to the evergreen pool

get.description: Per published destination that has metrics: the latest value of each metric with when it was read, and its snapshots oldest first (at most 500). A snapshot is stored only when a value changes. A null value means the network did not report it; a metric the network never reports is absent.

post.description: Unschedules and schedules again at a local time in a time zone, in one step. Every scheduled destination moves; a post with a destination publishing, verifying or waiting to retry is refused.

Freezes every draft destination and schedules it, at a local time in a time zone, as soon as possible, or at the next free slot of each destination's channel queue (422 queue_empty or queue_full names the channel). With repeat (instant only) the post becomes occurrence 1 of a series that starts at that local time (422 invalid_repeat; 409 when the post is already in a series).
Every scheduled or retrying destination goes back to an editable draft.

get.description: The repeat rule, its start in local wall time, the state and the local time of the next occurrence (null once the series has ended or stopped).

post.description: Sets a paused series active again, with the caller as its new owner: later occurrences are scheduled or submitted in their name. An active series is returned unchanged; an ended or stopped one is a conflict.
Ends the series: no further occurrence is created. Occurrences that already exist stay as they are.

get.description: Instance-wide: only for a session whose email is listed in KRONAUT_INSTANCE_ADMINS and who is an owner or admin of the workspace; never an API key. slo holds the publishing SLOs for the last 24 hours (day) and 7 days (week): onTimePct excludes provider 5xx, and a percentage is null when the window is empty. cron is the last run per task; stale means no run, or a start older than twice the task's interval, and detail is set only for a failed run. incidents are the open provider app incidents plus those resolved in the last 7 days, newest first, at most 50. apiVersions are the pinned provider API versions: warn at 90 days or fewer before the sunset, critical at 30 or fewer or after it.
